body:
Why It Matters Aircraft lessors moving into aftermarket parts, repair and end-of-life management signals a push toward owning whole-lifecycle asset value rather than leasing alone, tightening ties between lessors and maintenance suppliers.

Japanese firm ORIX Aviation has agreed to acquire AerFin, a Newport aviation company that has grown into a global supplier of aircraft engines, parts and maintenance services, in a deal worth about £475m . AerFin employs more than 230 people, operates from sites in the UK and around the world, and was founded by Bob James. It buys, sells, leases and repairs aircraft, engines and components, and says it serves more than 600 organisations. In 2025 it moved into a new purpose-built 116,000 sq ft facility at Indurent Park in Newport.

ORIX Aviation is the aircraft leasing arm of Japanese financial services group ORIX Group. For ORIX Aviation, the acquisition extends its activities beyond aircraft ownership and leasing into aftermarket services and end-of-life aircraft management, and the company said the combination would strengthen its capabilities across the whole lifecycle of an aircraft. AerFin was majority owned by private equity investor CataCap before the sale, and the deal marks CataCap's exit.

AerFin chief executive Simon Goodson called the acquisition a "defining moment" in the company's history and said support from ORIX Group would provide "the confidence and platform" to grow the business. ORIX Aviation chief executive James Meyler said AerFin had built "a leading aviation aftermarket platform" backed by extensive technical expertise and an international customer base. Founder Bob James said he was pleased to see the business move to "a long-term home" capable of supporting its next phase of expansion.

Shell will hold exclusive purchasing rights to about 150,000 tonnes a year of SAF, or equivalent HVO, from a planned $239 million Green Sky Manara plant at Port Nador, Morocco.

Surf Air Mobility reported third-quarter revenue of $36.5 million, up 25% year over year, while its net loss narrowed 25% to $20.4 million from $27.2 million.

The SEC has declared effective the Form S-4 for the Elroy Air and Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. VII merger, with a shareholder vote set for November 25, 2026.

Lufthansa Technik AERO Alzey and PSA Airlines signed a new multi-year agreement for maintenance and support of the carrier's CF34-8 engines, extending a relationship of more than 26 years.

Boeing rolled out the first 737 MAX 10, bound for WestJet, from its new Everett North Line on October 26, the first 737 variant built outside Renton since 1970.

Circularity Fuels, a startup that converts biogas into jet fuel, has raised a $7 million seed round to build a demonstration plant, CEO Stephen Beaton said.

IATA, which represents over 370 airlines, says sustainable aviation fuel could deliver up to 65% of the emissions cuts aviation needs to reach net zero by 2050.

As of November 5, 2026, no class action against Fly Alliance exists; its two reported cases are business disputes, with owner Zap Aviation's claims and minority member Christopher Colbath's Delaware suit.

A panel at ITIC Global 2026 in Istanbul examined how digital platforms are changing air ambulance quoting, with speakers arguing that the cheapest or fastest quotation is not always the best mission.

Wheels Up reported Q3 2026 revenue of $164.8 million, down 11% year over year, while ordering six Embraer Phenom 300E aircraft and securing a $100 million Delta credit facility.

Eve Holding reported a $58.1 million third-quarter 2026 net loss, up from $46.9 million a year earlier, as R&D spending rose to $48.3 million.

GlobalAir.com's cost guide puts used Pilatus PC-12 NG asking prices at $3.7 million to $5.1 million across ten listings, with a fixed annual cost of $281,000 and $2,011 per flight hour.

SkyDrive signed a tripartite MOU with Goyang Special City and Verty on Nov. 4, 2026 to prepare commercial eVTOL flights in Goyang, South Korea.

Air Charter Service won Best Charter Brokerage at the AsBAA gala in Hong Kong for the second consecutive year and received a European award on the same date.

Horizon Aircraft is building the Cavorite X7, a hybrid-electric VTOL aircraft for six passengers and a pilot, at Lindsay airport in Ontario, with certification possibly by 2030.

McKinney National Airport begins commercial service Nov. 11 with an Avelo Airlines flight to Fort Myers, one of five fall destinations, becoming the third commercial airport in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

Kazakhstan plans to add 1.5 million tons of jet fuel production capacity by 2030, Energy Minister Erlan Akkenzhenov said on November 4, 2026.

Heading365 has launched the CL30 FMS Trainer PRO for the Challenger 350/3500, its first business aviation product, with Aviation Academy Austria as launch customer under a multi-year agreement.

Miami International Airport plans a $1 billion D60 expansion replacing a regional boarding area at Concourse D with 17 contact gates, targeting a 2027 groundbreaking and initial 2030 completion, mainly financed through airport bonds.

Skyfly Technologies closed a $10 million seed round led by HICO Investment Group, with Archangel participating, to certify its Axe two-seat eVTOL and begin deliveries in 2027.

Moviation-operated VONAER became the first Korean private jet booking platform to join Avinode, the global charter marketplace, gaining access to more than 13,500 charter professionals worldwide.

Law firm Hamilton Locke advised Goodwin, the Columbus, Ohio private jet charter software developer, on its acquisition of STACK.aero, whose aviation CRM and operations platform joins Goodwin's business.

The International Aircraft Dealers Association and the American Society of Appraisers have formed an educational partnership that adds IADA's Quarterly Market Reports to ASA's aviation-specific valuation curriculum.

Airbus plans to raise its annual sourcing of aircraft components and services from India to USD 2 billion before 2030, up from about USD 1.6 billion currently.

Safran.AI will open its first international subsidiary in Singapore, a Centre of Excellence for industrial AI and automated MRO inspections, with about 50 staff expected within five years.

Bird & Bird published an article by associate Henry Everett setting out the key legal diligence and structuring issues buyers and sellers face in aviation mergers and acquisitions.

State and local officials broke ground on Oct. 3 on a new 14,000-square-foot terminal at Ponca City Regional Airport (KPNC) in Oklahoma.

UAE-based Prometheus Medical International said its operations involved approximately 1,000 flying hours over the past three to four months, three times the level recorded in the same period last year.

Four foreign firms, Menzies Aviation, Swissport, dnata and Çelebi Aviation Holding, were shortlisted for ground handling at Dhaka airport's third terminal, which is due to partially open on December 16.

Penang will receive a weekly winter charter from Warsaw starting 5 November, 19 flights through 25 March 2027, plus one-off charters from Busan on 12 November and Osaka on 30 December.

An ACMIWorld financing guide says ACMI start-ups need heavy capital before selling a first block hour and usually fund that phase with strategic equity before secured aircraft debt.

Indra Group has secured more than €40 million in new SESAR 3 innovation projects and will coordinate two of them, ARTEMISA and NEURON, building on 21 projects completed in phase 1.

Bombardier and BAE Systems signed a strategic agreement defining Canada's role in the GCAP sixth-generation fighter programme, months after Canada joined as an observer nation.

Castelion, a Torrance, California startup valued at $13 billion, is working to produce and scale low-cost hypersonic missiles, aiming to close a gap with China and Russia.
